title: Quasi-isomorphism from a good total resolution
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and let $M^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $\cdots \to A_2^\bullet \to A_1^\bullet \to A_0^\bullet \to M^\bullet \to 0$ be an exact augmented chain of cochain complexes of $A$-modules (exact in every cochain degree). Assume that for every degree $q$ the induced sequence $\cdots \to \Ker(d_{A_2}^q) \to \Ker(d_{A_1}^q) \to \Ker(d_{A_0}^q) \to \Ker(d_M^q) \to 0$ is exact. Form the total cochain complex $\operatorname{Tot}$ with $\operatorname{Tot}^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A_{-p}^q$ and the usual signed total differential. Then the augmentation $\operatorname{Tot} \to M^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

proof.text: For every cochain degree $q$, splice the short exact sequences $0 \to \Ker(d^q_{A_i}) \to A_i^q \to \Im(d^q_{A_i}) \to 0$ with the exact augmented rows and the exact rows of cycles. The resulting row $\cdots \to \Im(d^q_{A_1}) \to \Im(d^q_{A_0}) \to \Im(d^q_M) \to 0$ of images is exact. Splicing once more with $0 \to \Im(d^{q-1}_{A_i}) \to \Ker(d^q_{A_i}) \to H^q(A_i^\bullet) \to 0$ gives exactness of the cohomology row $\cdots \to H^q(A_2^\bullet) \to H^q(A_1^\bullet) \to H^q(A_0^\bullet) \to H^q(M^\bullet) \to 0$.

On $A_{-p}^q$ the total differential is the horizontal map plus $(-1)^p$ times the cochain differential (the repository's sign $d_I+(-1)^p d_{II}$), so its square is zero by cancellation of the mixed terms. Write a total cocycle of degree $0$ as a finite sum $x = x_n + \cdots + x_0$ with $x_i \in A_i^i$, where $n$ is maximal. If $n>0$, the total cocycle equation makes $x_n$ a cycle and makes its image in $H^n(A_{n-1}^\bullet)$ zero because that image is the boundary of $x_{n-1}$, up to sign. Exactness of the cohomology row of Step 1 lifts the class of $x_n$ from $H^n(A_{n+1}^\bullet)$; subtracting the total boundary of a lifting cycle $y \in \Ker(d^n_{A_{n+1}})$ makes $x_n$ a boundary $d z$ with $z \in A_n^{n-1}$, and subtracting $\pm$ the total boundary of $z$ makes $x_n = 0$. Repeating decreases the maximal index and terminates by finite support (the total complex is a direct sum), so every class is represented by a cocycle $x = x_0$; the same argument works in every degree.

Let $x_0, x_0' \in \Ker(d^0_{A_0})$ be two such cocycles whose images in $M^0$ differ by $d_M(m)$. Lift $m$ to $a \in A_0^{-1}$ by exactness of the augmented row; then $x_0 - x_0' - d_{A_0}(a)$ lies in $\Ker(d^0_{A_0})$ and maps to $0$ in $\Ker(d^0_M)$, so by exactness of the row of cycles it is the image of some $b \in \Ker(d^0_{A_1})$, whose total differential is that image. Hence $x_0 - x_0'$ is the total boundary of $b \pm a$. Conversely cohomologous cocycles have the same image in $H^0(M^\bullet)$, since the augmentation is a map of complexes. With Step 2 the augmentation induces a bijection on cohomology in every degree and is a quasi-isomorphism.
